stem: Which statement best distinguishes the hospital Child Protection Unit from the Department child protection service?

options.text: The Child Protection Unit is part of the Department helpline and mainly receives routine office-hours welfare calls
The Child Protection Unit is separate from FaCS and is staffed by child protection paediatricians or forensic paediatricians who can perform forensic medical assessment for suspected maltreatment
The Child Protection Unit mainly decides whether concerns are accumulative rather than significant
The Child Protection Unit replaces the need for clinical acumen when deciding whether there is risk of harm
The Child Protection Unit is the service that all mandatory reporters must notify instead of the Child Protection Helpline

explanation: The correct answer is B. The Child Protection Unit is a separate hospital-based service from FaCS and is staffed by child protection paediatricians or forensic paediatricians who can undertake forensic medical assessment for suspected maltreatment.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the Child Protection Unit is not part of the Department helpline and does not mainly receive routine welfare calls.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the Child Protection Unit is separate from FaCS and is staffed by child protection paediatricians or forensic paediatricians who can perform forensic medical assessment for suspected maltreatment.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because assessing accumulative concerns is not the main role of the Child Protection Unit.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because clinicians still need clinical acumen to assess risk of harm; the Child Protection Unit does not replace that judgement.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because mandatory reporting is made through the Child Protection Helpline, not directly to the Child Protection Unit.
